utterances.text: Across the road, I could see a person lying on the ground, a neighbour of mine from the street, an elderly man who was 65 years old. He was dead and he was lying in the grass.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Josip Kraljevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to his body?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: In the afternoon, on that very same day, Croat inhabitants from the village put him on a tractor-trailer and took him to the local cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And just so I understand what you said. You said in the afternoon on that day Croat inhabitants put him on a tractor-trailer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes. Under the escort of these armed Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, you describe seeing this group of people, Serbs you knew and those you didn't know, rounding up Croats. This group, could you describe how they were dressed?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: They were a mixed bunch. Some were wearing parts of police uniforms; others were wearing civilian clothes and military uniforms. It was mixed up. They didn't have complete uniforms. The articles of clothing they were wearing were of various kinds.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did they all have weapons?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: All of them had automatic and semi-automatic weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: The ones who were known to you, what ethnicity were they?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Serbian ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: How would you describe the general appearance of this group?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: They looked like a paramilitary formation. They were bedraggled, dirty.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And to be very clear, the group that you're talking about included more than the people that you specifically named before; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Are you able to estimate how many were in this group?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Well, about ten of them passed down my street. There are three or four streets so there must have been about 50 of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Were you called any derogatory names during this episode?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes. They called us Ustashas. They cursed our Ustasha mothers.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned seeing groups of Croats being rounded up. Where were they taken?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: They took them to the machine work-shop.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And is that also the co-operative Zadruga building?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes. It's the agricultural co-operative or the agricultural Zadruga.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And how were you able to see this happening?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: I was looking through the window. I live in that street in the centre, so I could see what was going on outside.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: In addition to this paramilitary group that you described, did you see anyone you believed to be a reserve or regular JNA soldier?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Well, before night fell, tanks entered the village, and about ten lorries with reservists, JNA reservists, arrived.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And did that happen on the 10th of October as well?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: There were lorries. Did any other type of military vehicles come to Lovas that evening?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: There were the tanks. They entered the village. About ten lorries of reservists, with equipment, military equipment arrived. They found accommodation, or they were billeted in the primary school in the centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And how far away is the primary school from the agricultural co-operative, the work-shop?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: It's about 200 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Where else were they housed?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: They were billeted at all -- or they were deployed at all the exits from the village. They set up check-points. The houses were mostly Croatian ones, the ones that were empty, and they entered the empty ones, if they were empty; and if they weren't, they drove the Croats out, and they took possession of their houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And how many Serb houses did they take over?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Not a single one.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, when Lovas was attacked on the 10th of October, 1991, how did the villagers defend themselves?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: They didn't. No resistance was mounted.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You described certain areas where the JNA was stationed. The check-points -- you said that they set up check-points. Who -- who was in charge of these check-points?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Well, the reservists. At all the exits from the village, they had set up some sort of check-points, and that's where they were deployed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you know if some Croats managed to leave the village of Lovas that day?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes. Most of the inhabitants, about 60 per cent of them, managed to flee that morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And do you know generally in what area of Lovas they lived to have been able to flee?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Mostly they lived in the peripheral parts of the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And where did you live?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: In the centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And why didn't you leave?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: The children were young. I was afraid for them. I didn't want to leave them behind. I was afraid that they might come to harm.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You described to the Trial Chamber the white sheets that had to be put on Croatian houses to identify them as Croatian houses. Were Croats identified in any other way?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes. All the Croats had to have white arm-bands on them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And where did you get these white arm-bands from?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Well, everyone took a white rag from their homes, and they had to wear these white rags, these arm-bands. The order was that we could not move around if we didn't have such arm-bands.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: When was that order given?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Immediately after they had entered the village, the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what did the Serb residents have to wear to identify themselves as Serbs?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Nothing. Those who were fit had to wear their uniforms, but they didn't have to wear any distinguishing marks of any kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did the order to wear the white arm-bands, was that only for the men, the Croatian men, in the village?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: No, it concerned all the Croats: Women and men. The Hungarians who were there also had to wear a distinguishing mark.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what was the distinguishing mark that they had to wear?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: The Serbs didn't have to wear any distinguishing marks.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You said: "The Hungarians who were there also had to wear a distinguishing mark." What distinguishing mark?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: They also had to wear a white rag, or white arm-band.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did there come a time that you learned that Croat villagers had been killed during the attack on Lovas on the 10th of October?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes. Two or three days later, I learned that about 20 people had been killed, including elderly persons and women. On the whole, the people killed were mostly elderly people who happened to be in the streets at the time. Most of them were killed by bombs or fire-arms -- by shells or fire-arms.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd like to turn your attention to what you described as being JNA soldiers. You described reservists. And you describe this paramilitary group. What -- did you learn what members of the paramilitary group called themselves?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: They said they were the Jovics or some of them were the Orlovi, the Eagles. Some of them were from the Dusan Silni group. I don't know to which groups the various individuals belonged, but these are the names that they used for themselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So you had the paramilitary group and then you had the people you described as JNA reservists. Were there any other armed formations present in Lovas?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: There was also the group called the Valjevci. These boys were all strong men, well armed, wearing camouflage uniforms. They were neat. It was a real army, they were real troops. It was some sort of a special unit, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So you describe JNA reservists, paramilitaries and this Valjevci. Were you able to estimate which group was the largest in number in Lovas?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: The JNA reservists.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You mentioned that JNA tanks came into Lovas on the 10th of October, 1991. Were they generally in Lovas?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: They were at all the exits from village. One was parked in the centre in front of my house. It was there day and night. It would go out at night and open fire, but these tanks were positioned at all the exits from the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: How did your daughters react to the tank that was in front of your house?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: They were afraid, very afraid. As soon as the engine was started, they would seek for a place to hide. They were very afraid.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd now like to ask you some questions about the Croatian homes in Lovas. What happened to the Croatian homes during and after the attack on the village?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: A lot of the Croatian houses were either set on fire or pierced by bullets. The window-panes were shattered. I had a neighbour, a woman, who was 70. Her house was set on fire on that day in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And how many Serb homes were set on fire or pierced by bullets?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What happened to the Croatian homes that were not set on fire or pierced by bullets?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: They were systematically looted. Everything of value was taken away. The cars that had been left behind in the courtyards or in the garages were driven away.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you know who burnt these houses, these Croatian houses?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: The Serb paramilitaries, both our locals and those who entered the village from somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And who looted these Croatian houses that you described?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: The Serbs, the paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What steps did you observe JNA soldiers, regular or reservists, take to stop the looting of Croatian houses?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: They didn't do anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what about the burning of the Croatian houses? What steps were taken to stop that?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Nothing. Again, nothing was done.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, were you free to move around in the village to go wherever you wanted during this time?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: No. We had to be marked by white pieces of cloth, and we had to work. We were given work assignments that we had to carry out and, otherwise, we were not allowed to move around the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Was there a curfew?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: From 1700 hours in the afternoon until 0700 in the morning. And during those hours, you were not supposed to move around. That was the curfew that we had to observe.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You said "we were given work assignments." Did that include just men?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Men and women. Croatian men and women.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did you have electricity in your -- in your house at this time?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Because there was just one generator in the centre. Two Croatian electricians were given the task to remove the fuses from our houses, Croatian houses, so we did not have electricity. The other part of the village where the -- the army and the Serb locals were living, they had electricity.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What were your work assignments? Let's talk about the first work assignment you had. What was it?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: I collected wood, twigs and branches, for the stove, for the bread stove.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did you get another assignment?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes. One morning, Djuro Prodanovic, a local Serb, approached me and told me that I would be required to go to Dubovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what were you supposed to do in Dubovac?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter's correction: The word was "drums."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was given a set of drums. I was asked to go to a cross-roads. I would be given a piece of paper with an inscription on it, and then I would drum to alert people's attention, and then I would read from that piece of paper what was written on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And who would give you the document to be read to others?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: From either Djuro Prodanovic or Savo Klisuric. They worked in the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Could you give us an example of an announcement that you had to make in this manner and describe how you went about doing it.

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: For example, everybody who had a tractor and a trailer were supposed to gather in front of the mechanical work-shop with their tractors and they were ordered to go out into the forest and gather wood.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So could you describe the process. You would get an announcement that was supposed to be read; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And where would you go with your drumming to alert people?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: I would go to all the cross-roads in the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And then what would happen?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: I would drum and people already knew what that meant. They would approach me. And then I would read out to them the most recent order that I was given.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what ethnicity were the people who came out to hear the announcements that you had to give?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Croats.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: The announcements that you had, did they usually have a name and a signature on them?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes. On the right-hand side, at the bottom, Ljuban Devetak's name was printed out, and there was his signature as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, which word do you use to describe what you had to read? Were they announcements or were they orders?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Those were orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And who was Ljuban Devetak? What was his role in Lovas village?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: He was referred to as the president of the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What was Ljuban Devetak's connection to Lovas?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: He is a native of Lovas. His parents lived there. He himself resided in Osijek.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And how did you learn that he held this position as the president of the village of Lovas?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: I heard that from conversations by the local Serbs who talked about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And did you come to learn in this manner as well the name of the local commander of the TO forces in the village?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And who is that?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Milan Radojcic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what do you mean by TO forces? Who -- who were those people?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Those were local Serbs who were armed. And when they moved around the -- the village, they always carried arms.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did you also learn in this manner the -- who the -- who was commanding the JNA after the takeover of Lovas village?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes. Passes were being issued to people who had to work in the fields outside of the village. They had to obtain passes and the passes were issued by the military command 4795 and they were signed by Marko Kovac, Captain Marko Kovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What colour were these passes?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Red.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And in the same manner that you described for the others, did you come to learn who the police commander was?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: The commander of the police was Milan Devcic. His father was a Croat and his mother was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: In carrying out your work assignments, did you learn that there were Croats detained in different parts of Lovas village?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes. They were detained in the basement of the town hall building where coal was kept and also in Boro Keser's house in the centre where the police station was.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So you describe that Boro -- is it Keser? Is that the name?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: That they were kept in his house in the centre where the police station was. Was it originally a police station before the takeover?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: No. It was a private house that used to belong to a Croatian person.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, I am going to test our video to see if it is working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Would this be an appropriate time, Ms. Biersay?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: If it suits the Chamber, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, we will take our second break now and come back at 12.45. The court usher will escort you out of the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now turning to tab 22, which is 65 ter number 6350. And before we play it, Mr. Witness, before the break, you described people being detained in the house of Boro Keser; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And also in the cellar of the municipal building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So I'd now like to play a short video-clip, and from this 65 ter number, it begins at minute 3 and 20 seconds, and we will play until minute 3 and 40 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: We're now paused at 3 minutes, 19 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, do you recognise the structure that's in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes. This house used to belong to a Croat, and this is where reservists were billeted.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: In Lovas; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: In Lovas, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now pausing at 3 minutes and 35 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you recognise the structure in that photograph, in that still?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: I do. This is Boro Keser's house where the police were billeted.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now turning to tab 23, if I may ask the Registry for 65 ter number 6351, page 16.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And, Mr. Witness, do you recognise the structure depicted in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes. This is the municipal building with the cellar, or a basement.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And if I may ask for some assistance so that Mr. Witness can mark the cellar that he just described.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And could you describe for the Trial Chamber your interactions with the detainees in that cellar.

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: When I was on the drumming duty, I also lit fire in the municipal building, and the coal was in the basement. The detainees were there. They would normally load my bucket with coal, they would pass it on to me, and then I would take it to the interior of the building where the stove was.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: At this time could we have the -- we tender the marked version of this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit Number P304. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I'll now like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Biersay, the video you showed, is it tendered?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: For now we'd like to have it marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's -- let's mark it for identification. Pending what, Ms. Biersay?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I believe that my colleagues will address other parts of the video and then we will tender the entire video. If there's no objection to it being tendered now, I'll do that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we object to -- to admittance -- to admitting of whole video in -- in the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: On what basis?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: That we didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Perhaps I could make a suggestion. Perhaps we can make a clip of the very, very short portion that we showed and tender that as -- as a separate exhibit, and then when my colleagues address additional parts, we may have to do the same thing if there's still an objection to tendering the whole video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So, for now we will tender the clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I thought you would say: And now we will object. Well, it's okay. It's a good idea. So you will provide with us a 20-second clip.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Yeah, let's give it an exhibit number, then, for the clip.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The video-clip, 20 seconds played in court, shall be assigned Exhibit Number P305. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed. Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I'd like to direct your attention to one week after the takeover, October 17th, 1991. On that day, did you also have drumming duties?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes. The idea was for all the male villagers to gather in front of the mechanics shop, all between the ages of 18 and 55 where -- and when they gathered, they would be told about some work that had to be done.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And when you say "the idea was for all the male villagers to gather," how -- how did you convey that idea? Was it something in writing that you had to read?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes, there was something I had to read out. I had been given a document by Djuro Prodanovic and I was supposed to that read that document to the people.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And when you said "all male villagers," do you mean both Serbs and non-Serbs were supposed to gather in front of the mechanics shop?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Croats were those who mostly came to such gatherings, and a few Hungarians that were still there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And the people who were told to report to the front of the mechanics shop, what was their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: They were Croats.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And do you remember the approximate time they were supposed to report to the mechanics shop?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: 1700 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what happened at 1700 hours?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: At 1700 hours, we were encircled by a group of the Valjevo men who were in the village. They searched us, one by one, and took us to the courtyard. There were two rows of benches in the courtyard that were prepared for us, and we were ordered to sit down on those benches.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Was this the first time you'd been searched or had you been searched before?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: That was the first time we were searched. They took away cigarettes, cigarette lighters, nail clips.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You said that you were ordered to sit down on the benches. What happened after you sat down on the benches?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: After that, Devetak, Ljuban Devetak, came, and he separated five people who had worked in the bakers shop. They normally worked night shifts. On that occasion, he separated the five men from the group and sent them to the bakery.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: How -- how many men, Croatian men, appeared at 5.00 as ordered in front of the mechanics shop?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: About 70.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: After these five were separated from the -- the group of 70, what happened next?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: They compiled a list, put our names down. They said we had to sit down on the benches and said we shouldn't turn around or get up. They said that we should just sit calmly on those benches, and above us there were automatic weapons and machine-guns on a sort of elevation above us.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And who was in charge of these automatic weapons and machine-guns that you describe?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: It was this group, the Valjevac group.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what happened next?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: We spent the entire night sitting on the benches. They would pass by us. They would pass through the rows and then hit us, punch us, or hit with us the rifle-butts, in the kidneys, in the head, in the stomach.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now turning to tab 23, which is 65 -- if I could please have 65 ter 6351 displayed, page 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you recognise the image in that photograph that appears before you?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes, that is the yard of the machine work-shop.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And if I could ask for some assistance for the witness in helping to mark the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd like you to draw two lines representing where you had to sit in the courtyard.

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And now if you could mark with an X the area that you described as being an elevation above you where there were automatic weapons and machine-guns aimed at you.

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: At this time we tender the marked version of this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit Number P306. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You described that you spent the entire night sitting on those benches and being beaten. Could you describe for the Trial Chamber what happened in the morning?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: In the morning, they entered the yard, Ljuban Devetak and the commander from the Valjevo group, and they tended to call him Bokser. I don't know what his name was. In any event, the -- they called out the names of the people and, as they did so, they would beat them with metal batons, with tubes, with knives, and they separated part of the men in the -- in the yard.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what part of the men was separated in the yard?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Well, the men who were sitting there, who spent the night sitting there with us, they called out Luketic Pero, Ante and Djuro. It's a father and his two sons. As they weren't there, they sent some men to fetch them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And when you say "they," because you say "they" a few times, are you referring to this same group?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes, the Valjevci, the group from Valjevo, Ljuban Devetak and this person called Bokser.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You said that they called out Luketic Pero, Ante and Djuro. Are those three people related?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes. Pero is the father and the other two are his sons.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And while some went to gather these three people who were missing from the roll-call, what -- what continued to happen?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: They continued calling the people who were sitting there out and they would beat them. In the meantime, these two men returned with Pero and his sons, and as soon as they arrived, they started beating one of them. Petronije stabbed Ante with a knife and he fell to the ground. He was bleeding. He went into a corner. They continued beating him with whatever they could.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what happened to the other two, the other son, and the father, Petar?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: They were beaten in front of us. They were also set aside, separated from this group of men who had previously been beaten up.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Then Ljuban and Bokser suddenly spoke to each other, tried to agree on something, and said that they would go outside the village to see if there were any Ustashas outside the village, in the vicinity of the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what happened after that discussion?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Gradually took us out, lined us up in two columns. We were on the internal side, and they were on the external side, to the left and right of us. We set off in a column to the centre and then we turned left down a slope that led to the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Approximately how many of you set off in these two columns?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: About 50 Croats.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And why only 50?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: The others remained there. They couldn't walk because they had been beaten up.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: After you turned left down the slope that led to the village, what happened?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Along the way we saw a man lying by a curve. He had been covered with some sort of a cover. He was dead. We arrived at the check-point, the reservists' check-point. They lifted the ramp and we passed through with the Valjevci, with the group from Valjevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what happened after you passed the -- through the check-point?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Well, they stopped us there, and then they lined up on the inside, and we were on the outside. The reason they gave for this was that if the Ustasha opened fire, they wanted us to be targeted. They wanted to avoid being targeted themselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: After there was this change in position, what was the next thing that happened?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: We continued down the road towards the exit from the village, and at a bend in the road, about 5- or 600 metres further down the road, Bosko Bodjanac stopped us. He'd been hit with a rifle-butt and he couldn't continue. They said he should continue or they would kill him. He said he couldn't. He stopped. We heard a burst of fire and that was it. We didn't dare turn around, and we continued as far as djetelina [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: At this time, I'm now turning to tab 20, and may I please ask the Registry to display 65 ter 6276.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: We continued as far as the clover field.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you recognise what village this aerial is of?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes, it's the entrance to Lovas.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And if I may ask for some assistance for the witness. 9

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: The first thing that I'd like to you do is to draw a big circle over -- around what you just said was the clover field.

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And if you're able to -- to see it on this screen, could you show to the Trial Chamber the route that you took from the mechanic shop towards the area that you just circled.

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: The -- the starting point of that red line that you made, what is at the very beginning of it?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: That would be the machine work-shop.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And are you able to see on this aerial the -- the place where the check-point was, approximately?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And could you number that as 1, please. Just with the number 1 in the -- at the check-point position.

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: At this time we tender the marked version of this aerial photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit Number P307. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: When did you realise that you were heading towards the clover field?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: When they stopped us there when we arrived in the area, they told us we should turn right and go up the slope towards the clover field. We were supposed to advance hand in hand, and we were supposed to trample on the field, on the clover field, to the left and to the right.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now directing your attention again to this, which is 62 -- 65 ter 6276, the unmarked version, could you again, in a very big circle, circle the clover field.

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And could you draw an arrow to show the direction in which they first asked you to walk.

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you. They -- you described how you were supposed to advance hand in hand and that you were supposed to trample the field to the left and to the right. Would you feel comfortable standing up and demonstrating that motion to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: No problem. I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You can try standing up and we'll see if your headphones will remain -- maybe they'll stay on. Let's try.

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: As we were advancing, we had to trample on what was in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You describe this as -- as a clover field. How -- was there, in fact, clover bushes on the field at the time?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes, clovers.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And how tall were those?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: About 30 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And did they explain to you why you had to do this?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: All they said is that we had to trample on what was on in front of us to make sure that no mines had been laid there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And did they tell you when you -- before you started doing the sweeping motion that you were looking for mines?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: They said that we should pass through and that we should trample on the clovers to make sure that no mines had been laid there. Or something of that sort.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, what happened next?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: When we arrived at the end, they sent us back. We turned to the left and set off in the other direction to do the same thing. We had to trample on the clovers, go to the other end.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And could you please draw an arrow in the second direction that you were asked to move in.

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you. So, Mr. Witness, I'd like to go back to make sure that I understood you correctly. You described walking down to the -- the clover field; correct?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And they -- the group that escorted you showed you in which direction to walk across the clover field; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you showed the Trial Chamber how that was done, and you held out your hands. Why -- why were -- did you hold out your hands in your demonstration?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And why were your hands out?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Well, because we had to link up in that way, by holding hands.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And when they told you to go across the clover field, they described to you how to do it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what happened?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: When we set off again, suddenly someone cried out, There's a wire. And you could hear an explosion. And in a second or two, fire was opened. They said if something happened we were not to lie down, but when they started firing -- well, whoever managed to do so, lied down and then when we lied down, when we were on the ground, we could hear the whizzing of bullets around us.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What -- when someone cried out, There's a wire, were you surprised by that?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes. We didn't see it. We only saw the clovers. We were surprised. There was a wire and then an explosion, so we were surprised.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did they explain to you before you started sweeping your feet back and forth that there were mines in that clover field?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It's asked and answered, and it is leading.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Well, I can ask it another way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: What did they tell you about mines, if anything, before you started sweeping your feet back and forth?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: They said we were going to sweep, do the sweeping motion, to make sure that no mines were there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And then there was the explosion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Fire was opened. At one point in time, they said that they should cease fire. Joco was wounded, that's what we heard was said behind our backs because a group of them was on the road and the other group was behind our backs, about 15 metres or 20 metres behind us. They started shouting, and they said that Joco was wounded and they ceased fire. We couldn't see that. We could only hear them. They were looking for bandages. He had been wounded in the leg. That's what we concluded from what they were saying. Then they said if anyone was healthy, if anyone could stand up, they should do so. Those of us who could stood up and they said whoever is wounded should raise their hands. This was done. And then --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: One minute. Sorry, Mr. Witness. Slow you down for a little bit. It is going very fast, and the interpreters have to keep up with us, okay? So we'll have to try to go just a little bit slower.

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You described that the -- there was an explosion, and that you heard shooting whizzing over your head, and that you heard screams; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And you laid down because you were afraid. You laid on the ground.

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes. Because -- we laid down because we were afraid, although they said we shouldn't. But we were afraid, so it was a reflex when we lay down.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did any vehicles go by you at this time?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: A military Pinzgauer arrived. It stopped. A JNA officer got out of it. He asked the men from Valjevo, the Valjevo group, about what had happened. They said that the men had come across mines and they said that the Ustasha had laid the mines. But he said that it wasn't the Ustashas, that the army had done this when they entered the village. He said that the wounded should be collected and taken to a doctor, and those who were in good health, he said, were to be returned to the village. He got back in the military vehicle and then drove away towards the exit from the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: After he left, what were you told to do, if anything?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: The Valjevo group ordered us to move on and to clear the mines. These were trip-wire mines so when you approach them you can see them. We had to sweep them. I myself deactivated five of them, took -- you take them off the base, take out the explosives, and you would then take these parts to the -- to the road, which is where they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: When you were engaged in the de-mining process, was there anyone still on the clover field?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: All the Croats who remained there, we continued to sweep aside the clovers, in fact, and to de-mine the mines that we came across.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And at that time, where were the wounded?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: The wounded and dead remained lying where they were, behind our backs.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: On the clover field or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: On the clover field.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, the dead laying on the clover field, do you know how they died?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Most of them sustained bullet wounds to the back.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: After you engaged in the de-mining of the -- the field, what happened next?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: A lorry arrived from the village. We helped take the wounded to the lorry, but while we were helping them, Mr. Stjepan Pejic stood on a mine and he was wounded in the leg. And Ivica Mujic, who was helping him, had also been wounded earlier on. He had been wounded by a -- a small mine, a very small mine, that we call Pasteta or paté; anti-personnel mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Was there anyone else who remained on the field while you were moving the -- the wounded?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: The dead bodies remained there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you know someone by the name of Josip Turkalj?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes. That lad was wounded in the spine. And he kept on saying that he did not have legs. We loaded him onto the lorry as well, but he succumbed to his wounds while he was being transported to Sid.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: You said "he kept on saying he did not have legs." Did he, in fact, have legs?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes, he did have legs. But I suppose that that part of his body was numb as a result of his wound in the spine.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what caused his wound in the spine, if you know?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: A bullet.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did you do anything else before leaving the -- the clover field at that time?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: We removed the mines or, rather, we deactivated them. We loaded our wounded friends into the lorry and then they took us back to the mechanical shop. On the way we saw Bosko Bodjanac's body at the curb where he was killed. In the shop, we were again assigned to various duties. I personally had to dig a trench in front of the school, which is centrally located in the village, so I saw one of those Valjevo guy whom they called Nikola driving in a white Golf, with Darko and Zeljko Palic as passengers in the car. Those guys are dead. We learnt a few days later that their bodies were discovered in the basement. They had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd like to take you back a step to when you arrived at the mechanical work-shop. You previously described that some of the men who were beaten and -- there were too beaten to go with you to the clover field. Were those men still at the mechanical work-shop?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: There was nobody there. There was a lot of blood, but they were nowhere to be seen. They were not in the courtyard, actually.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did you learn what happened to the men who remained behind while you went to the -- the minefield?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: All those men were killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Some friends from the village who went there a day or two later actually found their bodies in the basements and cellars of the houses where they were either shot dead or killed with hand-grenades.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: At this time, we'd seek the admission of the -- the marked version of the map [sic] currently on the screen, which is annotated 65 ter number 6276.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit Number P308. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now turning to TAB 10, which is 65 ter 2239. May I ask that that be displayed by the Registry, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you recognise this hand-drawn document?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: This is a road from the mechanical shop in the village to the clover field where all those mines were.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did you draw this map?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It will.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Directing your attention to the bottom of that map, the block marked number 1, do you recognise what that is on the map?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: This is the mechanical work-shop.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And directing your attention to number 2?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Number 2 is the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And who was stationed in the school in October 1991?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Reservists.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what is marked as number 3?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: The administrative building of the agricultural co-operative.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And number 4?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: The police.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And when you say "the police," whose house is that?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Boro Keser's house, a private house. But the police moved in, and they interrogated people there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And now directing your attention to number 5.

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Number 5 is a private house. Reservists were billeted there as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what is depicted at the number 7 position?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Number 7 is the curve where Bosko Bodjanac was killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what is the number 8 position?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Number 8 is on the clover field and denotes the direction that we had to take first.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what about number -- the number 9 position.

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Number 9 is the beginning of the minefield. The mines had been laying there in four rows.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And if I could ask for some assistance for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So that, Mr. Witness, if you could mark the -- the check-point that you described in your testimony.

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And could you mark that with a number 1, please. Actually, how about a letter A. Could you change it to an A.

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you. And directing your attention to the number 8, could you draw an arrow to follow the direction in which you were first asked to -- to walk. In the clover field.

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now number 10, what is that?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: That's another direction. When we were told to walk in that direction towards the mines.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And could you draw another arrow to depict that direction.

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Could you put these -- the first arrow that you did, could you put the letter B next to it, please.

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And C next to the second arrow.

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, while you were in the minefield, where were the Valjevci who were guarding you and the group?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: They were on the road, when we started walking in the first direction. And later on, some remained on the road, and some of them came behind our backs, some 15 to 20 metres away from us.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Could you draw an X to show the starting position where they were when you first started walking across the minefield.

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And could you now draw a line to show where they were behind your backs, as you just described to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And, if possible, could you put a D at the very beginning of that line so that we know that it's attached to the D.

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did -- did you have an opportunity to go where that X is yourself, as you were moving -- helping to move the wounded?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes. As a matter of fact, we went up there only when we brought the mines. As we removed the minutes, we went to the road. There were up there, on the road. That area, the road area, is somewhat higher up than the clover field. The difference is about 3 to 4 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And from where you stood, what could you see of the clover field?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: We could see that there were four lines that had been trampled on, where the soil had been trampled on. We could tell that that's where the mines had been laid.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what conclusion did you draw from seeing that?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: They knew that the mines were there. They could see the traces from where they were standing, and they could also see the mines from the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: To the -- where that number 9 is, there are four -- four rows. What -- what are those rows?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: The four rows of mines.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And is it from that area that you physically took mines from?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: At this time we would tender both the unmarked version of this hand-drawn map, as well as the marked version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Why would we need the unmarked version, Ms. Biersay?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Just so that the record is clear, Your Honour. Because I'm just concerned that maybe some of the -- the markings have obscured some of the lines there were there originally. But if the Trial Chamber is satisfied that it's clear enough, then the marked version is sufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I think it is. So let's admit and mark the marked version, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit Number P309. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: To be redacted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. [Interpretation] Witness, you told us that the place -- that from the place where they were, they were in a position to know that there were mines there. Do you know who had laid those mines in that field in the first place? Which army, which military was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A JNA officer confirmed that it was the military that laid the mines when they entered the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The same group, you mean, the same group that laid the mines also asked you to deactivate the mines, to remove them from the area; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The Valjevo men asked us to remove them, and the JNA officer who was standing there after the explosion told them that it had been the JNA that laid the mines when they first entered the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand that. But those who were behind you and who were watching and who knew where the mines were, were those the men who had laid the mines when they entered the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wouldn't know that. I don't know that it was them. I don't know whether it was them who laid the mines or somebody else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. My last question is this: The detained persons, those who were responsible for looking for the mines and sweeping the clover field, were they placed in some sort of a formation in order to be able to better detect and remove the mines?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I'm not sure how -- and, of course, I don't know how the last question of Judge Mindua have been -- has been translated into the witness's language, but definitely in the English language, there is a little confusion. Judge Mindua didn't ask whether they were placed in a certain formation but whether they had some training, special training, to be able to de-mine. So perhaps the witness could answer that question, how -- how -- how was it that you were able to deactivate the mines? I mean, I wouldn't know how to do it. How did you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One of the guys from Valjevo, he shouted at us that we should be careful of the wire and that we should pull the wire in an opposite direction from the mine and that's how you deactivated the mine. Then the mine could be removed. When it was removed, we were supposed to bring the mines up to the road to them. After that initial explanation and when we succeeded the first time, we were able to continue on our own.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So you were told how to do it. Now a follow-up question to that is: Why didn't they tell you that in the first place? Why did -- if you have any idea, why did they, first of all --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You don't know. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, without going back to the precise point in the transcript, my recollection is that at some point when you were being marched to the clover field, somebody from the -- as I recall and please correct me if I'm wrong, from the Valjevo -- this group had said it was the Ustashas who had laid the mines. And then later, of course, your explanation to Judge Mindua is that, at some subsequent point, one of the JNA officers said that they had laid the mines when they entered the village. Did I understand you correctly that at some point earlier in your march, one of this group who was taking you there had accused the Ustasha of having laid the mines?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Biersay, proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I'd like to, like the Trial Chamber, go back to the de-mining that you -- you did. You described that while you were laying on the ground that a vehicle, at some point, drove by and stopped; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And what kind of vehicle was it?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: It was a military vehicle known as a Pinzgauer.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And who, if anyone, came out of that vehicle?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: An officer of the Yugoslav army got out of that vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did someone from the Valjevo group say something to this JNA officer?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: They told him that it was the Ustasha that had laid the mines, to which he responded, No, it's not true. It was the army that laid the mines when they entered the village, and that the wounded should be transported to the hospital and that the rest of us who were not wounded should be brought back to the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So if I understand correctly, it was while you were still in the mine [sic] that you got the information from the JNA --

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Well, let me -- I know you know where I'm going but I have to finish for the record. So it's at this point that the JNA officer told you -- told the Valjevo group that the mines had been laid before by the JNA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And just so that I -- I understand correctly, it's after this officer stopped that you went about disarming -- collecting the mines and disarming them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Because you were told to.

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And who told you to?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: The guys from Valjevo. Because the officer got back into the car and drove off in the direction of the village, whereas the Valjevo guys made us disarm the mines and eliminate them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm looking at the time and I wonder if this would be a good place to stop for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We still have two minutes, but we could stop if you're moving to another topic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: If we have two minutes, I would like to turn to tab 22, which is 65 ter 6350, which is the video. And at this time we would play the segment from 13 minute and 32 seconds to 13 minute and 42 seconds. And that should take care of our two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And if we could stop and go back to the starting point of 13 minute and 32 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, do you recognise that view?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes. This is the minefield.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did it look differently in 19 -- in October 1991?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes. The monument was not there, and the only thing that was there was clover.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And if we could advance the time further.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And the direction that we're looking at, at 13 minute, 40 seconds, what is that?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: We can see the beginning of the minefield in the clover field, and we see the curve where Bosko Bodjanac was killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And from this perspective are we looking now towards the centre of the Lovas village?

utterances.speaker: GH-095
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And at this time we would also tender this short clip which we will prepare and give to the Registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: For the moment, Ms. Biersay, we only have the full video so you will provide us with the clips.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Correct. And I will give you the 65 ter numbers for that tomorrow for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Shall we admit and mark it right now or wait until tomorrow, Mr. Registrar? Let's give it a number, then.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit Number P310. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Witness, this is the end of your today's testimony. You're not released as a witness. You'll have to come back tomorrow morning. You're still under oath. That means that you can't discuss your testimony with anybody, and it also means that you're not allowed to speak to any of the parties. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The court usher will escort you out of the courtroom now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
